topic: Stable logical request identity to effect lineage and replayable semantic response continuity

facts: A proven EXPIRED_TAKEOVER can reconcile one dead V16 ADMITTED request to FAILED while preserving its durable request key.
The old holder remains fenced and exactly one effect attempt remains recorded.
V17 recovery reaches DONE_VALID and COMPLETE without duplicate effect execution.
Normal release/reacquire without EXPIRED_TAKEOVER and mismatched recovery holders are denied mutation authority.
The repaired path still lacks an immutable completed semantic response/result receipt for retry replay.

hypothesis: Execution-level V16 admission plus effect-generation fencing is sufficient to recover the exact prior effect/result for an exact retried ingress request.
counterhypothesis: Because one execution can admit multiple logical requests while effect-generation persistence is execution-scoped, exact request retry cannot select a unique prior effect/result unless a request-specific lineage or higher-layer response ledger exists.

searched_concepts: semantically equivalent response replay request effect lineage
counterevidence_search.result: No current target-repo code-search hit located a higher-layer typed response ledger keyed to the V16 request identity. Absence remains non-exhaustive and must not be promoted as proof of global nonexistence.

cross_branch_fusion.credential_semantics: credential_id and credential_fingerprint remain separate authentication-use provenance and must not define logical request identity across rotation
cross_branch_fusion.decision: Do not promote legacy credential-coupled V16 request_key_hash as the new request-to-effect lineage authority. Use the stable principal request identity or its promoted successor.

proposal: Persist one immutable stable logical request admission identity independent of rotatable credential instances.
Persist request-to-effect causal lineage as 1:N keyed by stable request_identity_hash because one logical request may legitimately cause multiple effects.

Persist one terminal semantic response receipt per logical request, referencing verified effect/outcome/re-entry receipts and carrying COMPLETE, RECONSTRUCTION_REQUIRED, FAILED or CANCELLED semantics without inventing historical bytes.

On exact retry, return or reconstruct the prior semantic result without re-executing already terminal effects; if outcome remains ambiguous, fail closed into reconciliation rather than guessing success/failure.
architecture_delta.rejected_shortcut: Enforcing a one-to-one execution-to-effect assumption is inconsistent with current follow-up request semantics and would hide the measured cardinality gap.
architecture_delta.rollback: No canonical schema/runtime mutation occurred in this receipt; reject the candidate and remove the stacked diagnostic branch if a stronger existing canonical response ledger is proven.

external_primary_evidence.source: AWS Builders Library - Making retries safe with idempotent APIs
external_primary_evidence.support: Caller-provided request identifiers support duplicate detection and semantically equivalent retry responses.
Idempotency tokens support retries without duplicate side effects and returning the prior response/result semantics.
Credential/token replay protection and sender constraints reinforce keeping credential instance/security provenance distinct from higher-level logical request identity.

strongest_remaining_counterhypothesis: A current canonical response/result ledger outside the inspected typed request/effect schema already binds stable logical request identity to all effects and terminal semantic response, making the proposed new lineage layer redundant.
next_falsifier: Compose the PR #329 stable request identity candidate with V16/V17 effect recovery in an isolated target test: admit two logical requests in one execution, bind distinct effect sets, rotate the credential for one retry, crash after effect terminalization but before response delivery, and require replay/reconstruction to select only the original logical request's verified effect set with zero duplicate effect attempts. This is an ordinary successor test, not a second GO OOB experiment.
